geometry_change: Radiator plates moved from ±0.067 m to +0.062/-0.170 m in x (radiator_plate_2 pushed further from the TTP stack); connecting copper straps (part_7, part_10) lengthened from 0.018 m to 0.067 m span to bridge the gap; the foam enclosure (component11/foam_box in the baseline) is absent from this STEP export, so the assembly is bare rather than boxed.
note_heat_source: Same heat_flux/area artifact as the baseline: q=17943 W/m2 applied to ymax of interface_plate over patch area 0.003667 m2 (> TTP contact area 0.00209 m2) gives an effective applied Q=66 W instead of the nominal 37.5 W design duty. Kept identical to the baseline manifest for a like-for-like comparison.
interpretation: Spacing the radiators farther apart (longer copper straps) has a negligible effect on peak component temperature (<0.1 K) and none on total radiator rejection at 30 km, because sky-sink radiation is set by local surface temperature/emissivity/area, not radiator position. The longer straps do carry noticeably less conductive power (~21% lower interface flux at the strap-to-radiator joint) for the same applied heat load — consistent with added series conduction resistance along the longer copper path — but the assembly compensates with a slightly larger driving ΔT along the strap rather than a hotter TTP stack, so the net thermal margin to any component limit is essentially unchanged from the baseline.
caveat: This variant's STEP export omits the foam enclosure present in the baseline (component11/foam_box_outer), so it is not a pure radiator-spacing-only comparison — the bare assembly also loses whatever insulating/radiative moderation the foam box provided. Energy balance is not fully closed (applied Q=66 W vs total logged external+interface losses well below that) at 500 iterations, same as the baseline; both runs are treated as adequately converged for design comparison (residuals <=0.02) rather than exact energy closure, per the baseline's own acceptance precedent.
